excerpts.text: | John Jumper |

**John Michael Jumper** (born 1 January 1985)[[1]](#cite_note-w007-1)[[2]](#cite_note-nobel_bio-2) is an American chemist and computer scientist. Jumper and [Demis Hassabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demis_Hassabis "Demis Hassabis") were awarded the 2024 [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry") for [protein structure prediction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_structure_prediction "Protein structure prediction") along with [David Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Baker_(biochemist) "David Baker (biochemist)") for computational protein design.[[3]](#cite_note-NobelPrize_2024_Summary-3)[[4]](#cite_note-NobelPrize_2024_Press_release-4)

In 2024, Jumper and [Demis Hassabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demis_Hassabis "Demis Hassabis") shared half of the [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry") for their protein folding predictions, the other half went to [David Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Baker_(biochemist) "David Baker (biochemist)") for computational [protein design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_design "Protein design").[[3]](#cite_note-NobelPrize_2024_Summary-3)[[4]](#cite_note-NobelPrize_2024_Press_release-4)

excerpts.text: [The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](http://www.kva.se/en/) has decided to award the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025 to

**Susumu Kitagawa**, **Richard Robson** and **Omar Yaghi** are awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025. They have developed a new form of molecular architecture. In their constructions, metal ions function as cornerstones that are linked by long organic (carbon-based) molecules. Together, the metal ions and molecules are organised to form crystals that contain large cavities. These porous materials are called metal–organic frameworks (MOF). By varying the building blocks used in the MOFs, chemists can design them to capture and store specific substances. MOFs can also drive chemical reactions or conduct electricity.
**Omar M. Yaghi**, Born 1965 in Amman, Jordan. PhD 1990 from University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, USA. Professor at University of California, Berkeley, USA.
